name: Pudding
description: Pudding is a creamy, sweet dessert that is popular with humans but can be quite risky for cats. While a plain, starch-based pudding isn't immediately poisonous, it offers no nutritional value and is packed with sugar that cats don't need. The real danger comes from the extra ingredients used to make different pudding flavors. Chocolate pudding is highly toxic because it contains theobromine, a compound that can cause vomiting, muscle tremors, and heart issues in cats. Sugar-free puddings often use an artificial sweetener called xylitol; while xylitol is extremely dangerous to dogs, current research (ASPCA, Merck, and a peer-reviewed feline study) shows cats are not affected by it and do not develop the hypoglycaemia or liver injury seen in dogs. Additionally, most puddings are made with milk or cream. Once cats grow up, they lose the ability to easily digest lactose (the sugar in milk). Eating dairy-based pudding will likely give your cat an upset stomach, gas, or diarrhea. Because of these hidden dangers, it is best to never give your cat pudding. If your cat gets into chocolate or sugar-free pudding, contact a veterinarian immediately.
safetyNotes: Chocolate pudding: TOXIC — contains theobromine; even small amounts can cause vomiting, tremors, and cardiac effects

Sugar-free pudding: xylitol is dangerous to dogs but does NOT affect cats — ASPCA, Merck, and a peer-reviewed feline study confirm cats are not at risk of xylitol-induced hypoglycaemia or liver injury
Dairy-based pudding: causes lactose-related vomiting and diarrhea in most adult cats
Plain starch-based pudding without toxic additives: not toxic, but very high in sugar and provides no nutritional value
Check the ingredient list before assuming a pudding is safe; chocolate exposure requires immediate vet contact

symptoms.name: Gastrointestinal Upset (Diarrhea and Vomiting)
symptoms.onset: Within a few hours (typically 8 to 12 hours for diarrhea to peak).
symptoms.notes: Most adult cats are lactose intolerant because their bodies no longer produce sufficient amounts of the enzyme lactase after weaning1. When the undigested lactose from the milk or cream in the pudding reaches the colon, it ferments and draws in water, causing stomach upset and loose stools.

symptoms.name: Pancreatitis
symptoms.onset: Progressive (can develop hours to days after consuming a high-fat meal).
symptoms.notes: Standard puddings are often made with heavy cream, butter, or whole milk. Ingesting rich, high-fat human foods can overload a cat's digestive system and trigger pancreatitis, a painful and potentially life-threatening inflammation56. Symptoms from Chocolate Pudding (Methylxanthine Toxicity)

symptoms.name: Restlessness, Muscle Tremors, and Seizures
symptoms.notes: Chocolate pudding contains theobromine and caffeine, which are toxic methylxanthines78. These compounds severely overstimulate the central nervous system, causing the cat to become restless and potentially progress to muscle tremors, seizures, and coma.

symptoms.name: Tachycardia and Cardiac Arrhythmias
symptoms.notes: The methylxanthines in chocolate also overstimulate the cardiovascular system, leading to dangerous, irregular heart rhythms that can ultimately result in cardiac arrest.

symptoms.name: Vomiting, Diarrhea, and Increased Thirst
symptoms.notes: Often the earliest signs of chocolate poisoning, theobromine and caffeine act as GI irritants and mild diuretics, causing the cat to lose bodily fluids rapidly79. Symptoms from Sugar-Free Pudding (Xylitol Exposure)

symptoms.name: Hypoglycemia and Liver Failure (Theoretical / Rare in Cats)
symptoms.onset: 15 to 30 minutes for a drop in blood sugar; 1 to 3 days for signs of liver injury
symptoms.notes: Xylitol is an artificial sweetener commonly used in sugar-free puddings. While it causes a massive, life-threatening release of insulin and acute liver failure in dogs, cats appear to be naturally resistant to xylitol toxicity.
